SEARCH
Package com.egradx.auth.config

Class EgradxAuthAutoConfiguration

java.lang.Object
com.egradx.auth.config.EgradxAuthAutoConfiguration
@AutoConfiguration(before={org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.data.jpa.JpaRepositoriesAutoConfiguration.class,org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.orm.jpa.HibernateJpaAutoConfiguration.class}) @AutoConfigurationPackage(basePackageClasses=EgradxAuthPackageMarker.class) @ComponentScan(basePackages="com.egradx.auth") @EnableCaching @EnableMethodSecurity public class EgradxAuthAutoConfiguration extends Object
Wires up egradx-auth. Picked up automatically by any app that depends on this jar (see META-INF/spring/org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.AutoConfiguration.imports).

Requires a KeyPair bean named jwtSignatureKeyPair on the classpath — that's supplied by egradx-tls-provider's RSAKeyInitializer, which egradx-auth depends on directly, so nothing extra needs to be added for that to work. It does still need egradx.security.crypto.keystorePath / egradx.security.crypto.passphrase (read by that module) and egradx.auth.issuer-uri (read by this one) configured by the host app.

    • egradxAuthDefaultSecurityFilterChain

      @Bean @ConditionalOnMissingBean(org.springframework.security.web.SecurityFilterChain.class) public org.springframework.security.web.SecurityFilterChain egradxAuthDefaultSecurityFilterChain(org.springframework.security.config.annotation.web.builders.HttpSecurity http, EgradxAuthenticationFilter egradxAuthenticationFilter, EgradxAuthenticationEntryPoint egradxAuthenticationEntryPoint, EgradxAccessDeniedHandler egradxAccessDeniedHandler) throws Exception
      Depending on egradx-web-security (for token verification) transitively pulls in spring-boot-starter-security's OAuth2-resource-server bits, which makes Spring Boot's own "authenticate every request" default security auto-configuration active on the classpath — that would 401/403 every request in the whole host app, including egradx-auth's own /register and /login, before any of our code even runs.

      This bean exists purely to opt back out of that surprise default so egradx-auth works out of the box. It is intentionally permissive, not a real security policy — EgradxAuthenticationFilter still runs (wired in below) and populates real identity/authorities for @PreAuthorize to check on whatever business controller a host app builds; this chain just doesn't gate entry on its own. The moment the host app defines its own SecurityFilterChain bean — which any real deployment should — this one backs off automatically, and the host app is responsible for adding .addFilterBefore(egradxAuthenticationFilter, UsernamePasswordAuthenticationFilter.class) to its own chain the same way this one does.

      Throws:
      Exception
